content.text:
SrNdCoO4 (mp-1218146) is the only candidate that fits the pattern, but its simulated peaks sit 0.4–1° away from the observed ones, so this is a match by peak pattern, not an exact fit. I ran simulations for all nine candidates.

- **Observed peaks:** about 14.15, 17.85, 21.7, 24.35, 28.6, 31.8 (strongest, 100), 33.2 (47), 43.35, 44.35, 47.65 and 58.45° (51). There are also weaker ones near 40.1, 55.75 and 57.05°.
- **SrNdCoO4:** its simulation has the same sequence of peaks, with a strong doublet at 31.0 and 32.15°. The observed peaks are shifted from these, though not all in the same direction. The doublet is about 0.8–1° higher, while the 24.8° peak is about 0.45° lower. That fits uneven stretching of the unit cell (anisotropic lattice strain). That reading is my assumption, not something I checked.
- **Pattern type:** the observed peaks (≈14.1, 28.6, 31.8, 33.2, 43–44, 47.7, 58.5°) also follow the pattern typical of a layered K2NiF4-type cobaltate. That supports the match.
- **The other candidates don't fit:**
  - CaAgO2 and CaMoO3 put their strongest peaks where the observed pattern has none.
  - The SiO2 and NaMn2O4 main peaks (21.2° and 17.8°) only line up with weak observed features.
  - For Bi2BO5, Ba2Mn2Sb2O and SrEuZrSnO6, the main peak or the rest of the series doesn't match.
- **Possible second phase:** TaGaO4 can't be fully excluded. Its peaks at 17.9, 24.5 and 31.6° coincide with observed ones. But its expected 35.7/36.3° peaks are absent, and they would be weak enough to hide in noise anyway. I left it out.

{"present": ["mp-1218146"], "confidence": 0.6, "note": "The observed peaks follow SrNdCoO4's simulated sequence but sit 0.4-1 degrees off in mixed directions (assumed anisotropic strain), and a minor TaGaO4 phase cannot be fully excluded."}
